transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because I just can't keep my mind on a task long enough to finish it anymore. It's happening even when it's really important. I do computer support, and... well, I'll start tracing a client's network problem, and ten minutes later I'll realize I've reread the exact same log entries three times. And I still don't know what they actually say. It's just getting impossible to get through my work.
Has this trouble concentrating been present for as long as you can remember?

Yeah, pretty much. My mother actually still jokes about it. She says that back in grade school, my report cards always said I was a bright kid, but... well, that I never stayed in my seat. And they'd always mention that I blurted out answers in class, or that I somehow managed to lose my homework even when I had actually done it. So, yeah, it's been an issue since I was young.
Do you still have trouble sitting still?

Yes, definitely. It's... well, I'm always moving something. When I'm sitting with a client, or even in a chess meeting, my leg is usually bouncing. Or I'm clicking a pen, or just turning a cable tie over and over in my fingers. I usually don't even realize I'm doing it until somebody finally gives me that look.
Do you often find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things?
No, not really. I mean, I get stressed when I'm falling behind at work because I can't focus, but I wouldn't say I'm a worrier. I don't sit around stressing about all sorts of different things, no.
